text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
ADEVARUL
- Prices for energy might remain unchanged in 1997, the paper quotes the new boss of Renel RA electricity authority as saying.
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Trade unions in the farming sector threatened to stage a protest rally in Bucharest using tractors and animals.
- The Dutch government will give Renel a $1.0 million loan to upgrade its equipment and cut pollution.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The opposition Party of Social Democracy plans to bring some 60 amendments to the budget bill, the paper says.
ADEVARUL
- Farmers will get subsidised credits starting March 26.
- Some 900 workers at the Ghelari copper mine went on strike.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Water consumption in Romania is four times higher than in the Western countries, said Viorel Raicu, state secretary at the Environment Ministry.
- The Senate's economic commission asked the government to cut income and profit taxes.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The state television could stop broadcasts by June following shortage of funds to pay for the carrier wave.
- Prosecutors started investigations into alleged illegal sales of ships owned by the state-run fishing fleet.
ADEVARUL
- Renel is determined to cut electricity supplies to all bad debtors, Renel's new boss Aureliu Leca said.
- The Senate's health commission asked for an extra 2,000 billion lei to be allocated to the health sector, bringing its budget to four percent of the GDP.

- Prosecutors reopened investigations in the case of Bucharest nightclub owner Constantin Constantin, suspected of pimping and robbery. Constantin was arrested in 1995 but eventually released for lack of evidence.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The European Christian Democratic Union has passed a resolution supporting Romania in its bid to join NATO.
-- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
